segments.source: Density = number ÷ area. A zone exceeds comfortable capacity if density is greater than the stated threshold.
Task.
What is the visitor density, and is the zone above the stated comfortable capacity?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Density=56÷8=7.00 visitors/hectare. 2. Compare 7.00 with the threshold 9.
Answer.
7.00 visitors/hectare; within capacity.
Knowledge takeaway.
Totals and densities answer different questions; always identify the denominator.
Formal model.
Ratio density=N/A followed by threshold comparison.
N6. Land use and spatial compatibility
Problem 901. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 1
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. The school must be on an end plot. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. The school is on an end plot. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Answer.
A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
Problem 902. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 2
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. The school must be on an end plot. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 10 members, requires at least 6 present for quorum, and 8 are present.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: is quorum met?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=school, B=homes, C=park, D=factory. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. The school is on an end plot. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: compare 8 with 6; 8≥6 is true.
Answer.
A=school, B=homes, C=park, D=factory is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
Problem 903. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 3
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. The school must be on an end plot. Cross-domain check: researchers collected 9 reports, but 4 are exact duplicate copies that add no new independent information.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, independent reports = total reports − duplicate copies.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: how many non-duplicate reports remain?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=factory, B=park, C=homes, D=school. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. The school is on an end plot. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: 9−4=5 independent reports remain.
Answer.
